objectives: Students will choose a safe, appropriate anesthetic protocol for routine small animal and small exotic animal cases, including pediatric and geriatric animals.

Students will choose a safe, appropriate anesthetic protocol for more critical small animal cases, including patients with cardiac, pulmonary, endocrine, renal, hepatic, GI, neurological, ophthalmic disease, and ASA sta…
Students will become familiar with the techniques of anesthetic monitoring and be able to determine the appropriate level of monitoring for each case.
Students will anticipate the common complications seen under general anesthesia, and know how to prevent, recognize, and treat them.
Students will know how to appropriately use anticholinergics, sympathomimetics, anti-dysrhythmics, crystalloids, colloids, blood products, and oxyglobin perioperatively.
Students will know the indications and techniques for IPPV.
Students will know how to appropriately stabilize and perioperatively manage patients for emergency anesthesia (GDV, c-section, acute abdomen, trauma, airway emergencies.
Students will know how to manage pain in small animal and exotic patients, including the use of regional and local blocks.
